title: (Shriek) is an isomorphism when (Push) is one
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-derived-lower-shriek-hom], if (Push) for the proper part $g$ of the
chosen compactification of $f$ ([def-sfb-derived-push-hom]) is an isomorphism, then (Shriek)
$T^Y\circ Rf_!\to Rf_!\circ T^X$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $I_\Lambda=D(i_!)$ for the source coefficients and $I_{\Lambda'}=D(i_!)$ for the target coefficients, and put $P_\Lambda=R(g_*)$, $P_{\Lambda'}=R(g_*)$. By [def-sfb-derived-push-hom], the hypothesis gives a natural isomorphism $\beta:T^Y\circ P_\Lambda\longrightarrow P_{\Lambda'}\circ T^Z$. By [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso], there is a natural isomorphism $\sigma:T^Z\circ I_\Lambda\longrightarrow I_{\Lambda'}\circ T^X$. The definition [def-sfb-derived-lower-shriek-hom] says that, after the canonical reassociations, (Shriek) is $v\circ u$, where $u_K=\beta_{I_\Lambda K}$ and $v_K=P_{\Lambda'}(\sigma_K)$ for every $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph: expand the composite and its inverse

proof.text: The natural transformations $u$ and $v$ from step 1 have inverses with components $u^{-1}_K=(\beta^{-1})_{I_\Lambda K}$ and $v^{-1}_K=P_{\Lambda'}(\sigma^{-1}_K)$. Naturality is respectively the naturality of $\beta^{-1}$ evaluated on $I_\Lambda$ of a morphism and functoriality of $P_{\Lambda'}$ applied to the naturality equation for $\sigma^{-1}$. The two inverse equations for $u$ are those of $\beta$ evaluated at $I_\Lambda K$. For $v$, one has $v^{-1}_K\circ v_K=P_{\Lambda'}(\sigma^{-1}_K\circ\sigma_K)=P_{\Lambda'}(1)=1$ and $v_K\circ v^{-1}_K=P_{\Lambda'}(\sigma_K\circ\sigma^{-1}_K)=1$. Thus both inverse equations hold as equations of natural transformations, component by component.

source.place: Proof, sole paragraph: expand the composite and its inverse

proof.text: For the suppressed-associator expression $v\circ u$, use $u^{-1}\circ v^{-1}$ as inverse: $(u^{-1}\circ v^{-1})\circ(v\circ u)=u^{-1}\circ(v^{-1}\circ v)\circ u=1$ and $(v\circ u)\circ(u^{-1}\circ v^{-1})=v\circ(u\circ u^{-1})\circ v^{-1}=1$. To retain the actual parenthesization, denote the canonical reassociations before, between and after the two whiskered factors by $w_0,w_1,w_2$ (an absent reassociation is an identity), so that $S=\mathrm{(Shriek)}=w_2\circ v\circ w_1\circ u\circ w_0$. Set $Q=w_0^{-1}\circ u^{-1}\circ w_1^{-1}\circ v^{-1}\circ w_2^{-1}$. Associativity gives $Q\circ S=w_0^{-1}\circ u^{-1}\circ w_1^{-1}\circ(v^{-1}\circ v)\circ w_1\circ u\circ w_0=w_0^{-1}\circ(u^{-1}\circ u)\circ w_0=1$, where the first equality cancels $w_2^{-1}\circ w_2$ and the second cancels $w_1^{-1}\circ w_1$. In the other order, cancelling $w_0\circ w_0^{-1}$ gives $S\circ Q=w_2\circ v\circ w_1\circ(u\circ u^{-1})\circ w_1^{-1}\circ v^{-1}\circ w_2^{-1}=w_2\circ(v\circ v^{-1})\circ w_2^{-1}=1$, using $w_1\circ w_1^{-1}=1$. Thus $Q$ is the inverse of (Shriek).
